correctness.rationale: The embedded Markov chain at vacancy sizes (a,b,c) has AB,AC,BC rates wab,ac,bc. Invariant c=a+b+2K and positive c whenever a+b>0 imply terminal (0,0,2K) and R=2K exactly. Rare-event hazard p=w ab/[c(a+b)+wab]<=w/4 gives binomial stochastic domination, K=O_P(1) and uniformly bounded exponential moments when nw->lambda finite. For imbalance d=a-b, conditional drift of d² <=1 and Doob/optional-stopping controls max|d|/n; conditional on s>=delta n, hazard n p→lambda/4 uniformly in probability. Uniform-variable coupling across ~2n initial events gives Poisson((2-delta)lambda/4), with tail AB probability <=delta lambda/4. delta→0 and exponential-moment bound give all moment convergence. Independent exact rational reduced-state recursion for n=3,6,10,18 and finite comparisons point toward the predicted mean and vacancy law; finite cases are not an asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: PASS. Earlier October 26 2026 published full text proves a superficially similar Poisson terminal-jamming correction on unweighted tripartite graphs with a superlinearly dominant class M_n≫n and two minorities n, whereas here c=2n initially and depletes on the same scale as a+b while AB rate is w_n~lambda/n. The earlier regime cannot be specialized or rescaled to these simultaneous balanced-capacity/weak-channel dynamics. Pippenger 1989 addresses sparse regular or tree-like graphs, not this dense weighted tripartite boundary. No matching prior exact even-Poisson law was found in targeted Resultary or published-abstract searches.
